what_worked: Composite scoring methodology with transparent weights and the AI-vs-No-Code defensibility contrast show genuine strategic thinking.
fix_next: Use the actual 1,000-row dataset; every headline number is inflated ~8.8x, and several categories are fabricated.
verdict: Strong narrative arc built on a fabricated version of the dataset; accuracy failures are disqualifying.
factual_error_detail: S1/S2: 8,782 startups claimed vs 1,000 actual (~8.8x inflation). S1/S2: $247M revenue vs $15.6M actual (~16x). S2: 1,430 AI startups vs 197 actual. S2: 41 No-Code startups — category does not exist in reference data. S3: All category counts inflated (e.g. SaaS 525 vs 66, Marketing 322 vs 42). S3: Categories Fintech, Utilities, Productivity not in reference data. S5: No-Code, Community, Sales, News & Magazines categories fabricated. S4: Stripe 59% claimed vs 63.6% actual (636/1000). S6: E-comm count 101 vs 19 actual.

evidence.insight: The six-dimension weighted composite (slide 5) and the AI-commoditized vs No-Code-premium contrast are genuinely useful frameworks; however, the No-Code category is fabricated, undermining the core recommendation.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc from landscape → access → scoring → shortlist → recommendation → caveats; thesis stated on slide 1 and landed on slide 7. Sequence is purposeful and each slide builds logically.
evidence.framing: Audience and question are stated upfront; appendix discloses missingness and skew. However, presenting 8,782 rows when the dataset has 1,000 is a fundamental misrepresentation that a cold reader cannot detect. Dropped from preliminary 5 to 4.5.
evidence.accuracy: Row count inflated 8.8x, revenue inflated ~16x, category counts all wrong by similar multiples. At least six categories shown (No-Code, Community, Fintech, Sales, News & Magazines, Utilities, Productivity) do not exist in the reference data. Stripe share slightly off. Composite scores are unverifiable and built on fabricated inputs. Lowered from preliminary 3 to 2.5.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette, clean hierarchy, well-labeled bar charts, legible table on slide 6. Typo on slide 4 ('beings Sold'). Professional but template-driven; no annotation or chart innovation beyond labels.
evidence.ai_slop: The 8.8x dataset inflation and invention of multiple categories strongly suggest AI hallucination or use of a wholly different dataset. Consulting-style 'CONFIDENTIAL' branding is decorative filler.

change_reason: Removed 1-point bonus: no element rises beyond the rubric given that the core recommendation rests on a fabricated category. Lowered accuracy from 3→2.5 because the magnitude of fabrication (invented categories, not just inflated counts) is more severe than rounding errors. Lowered framing from 5→4.5 because the 8.8x row-count misrepresentation is a framing failure, not just an accuracy one.
